title: An old trend refuses to leave
description: Your last-hour trending counter uses sixty one-minute buckets and a running total per tag. At each minute boundary it deletes the oldest bucket, but a hashtag with no recent activity remains near the top all afternoon. What is missing from expiration?

options.text: Reset every tag's total to zero on the hour.
options.explanation: That creates tumbling-window behavior and throws away still-valid events from the preceding hour.

options.text: Increase the cached list's TTL so readers stop seeing frequent changes.
options.explanation: Caching cannot repair incorrect counter state and would make the stale trend last even longer.

options.text: Subtract the expiring bucket's counts from running totals, then update the ranking before publishing the next list.
options.explanation: Deleting storage alone does not undo its contribution to accumulated totals. Sliding windows require both addition and subtraction, and the top-K structure must reflect decreases too.

options.text: Repartition by a random event ID so old events spread evenly across shards.
options.explanation: Changing partitioning does not remove expired contributions and would break the simple key-sharded local-top-K merge guarantee.
